title: Molina departs from both; sufficient aid given to all
source_text: LXXVIII. Caeterum a sententia Jansenii Iprensis, & recentiorum etiam Thomistarum, multum distat doctrina Ludovici Molinae Jesuitae celeberrimi, quem plures alii sequuntur. Quod ut clarius pateat, summa sententiae illius, circa gratiam efficacem atque sufficientem, ex scriptis ejus est breviter repetenda. Ille ergo non vult ullum gratiae auxilium sufficiens dici, praeter illud, quo posito, nihil amplius ex parte Dei praerequiritur, ut actio reapse sequatur. Atque hoc modo sufficiens gratiae auxilium docet a Deo concedi, tam iis qui bene non agunt, neque se ad Deum convertunt, quam iis qui convertuntur & bene operantur.
pass_a_gloss: LXXVIII. However from the opinion of Jansenius of Ypres, and of the more recent Thomists also, the doctrine of Luis Molina the most celebrated Jesuit, whom many others follow, differs much. Which that it may appear more clearly, the sum of his opinion, about efficacious and sufficient grace, is briefly to be repeated from his writings. He therefore does not will any help of grace to be called sufficient, besides that, which being posited, nothing more on the part of God is prerequired, that the action actually follow. And in this way he teaches that a sufficient help of grace is granted by God, as much to those who do not act well, nor convert themselves to God, as to those who are converted and work well.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXVIII. The teaching of the most celebrated Jesuit Luis de Molina, whom many others follow, is far removed from the view of Jansenius of Ypres and of the recent Thomists as well. To make this clearer, the substance of his view on efficacious and sufficient grace should be briefly restated from his writings.

He will not have any aid of grace called sufficient except one which, once given, requires nothing further on God's part for the action actually to follow. In this sense he teaches that God grants sufficient aid of grace both to those who do not act well and do not turn to God and to those who are converted and act well.
